At the first later cycle with !(req.fire||update.valid): usefulCanReset=1, set 127 is written, resetFinish = usefulCanReset && resetSet===127 is 1, resetSet wraps to 0 and needReset := false (IttageTable.scala:187-188). Sweep is over. Set 5 bank 0 of table 0 still has usefulCnt=1: the second pulse produced a sweep of exactly one set index (127) instead of 128. Generally, a pulse arriving with needReset=1 and resetSet=k>0 clears only sets k..setsPerBank-1 after the pulse; sets 0..k-1 (including any whose useful bit was re-set between their sweep write and the pulse) are not cleared until a third saturation (another 255 net failed allocations) that arrives while needReset=0. Meanwhile those sets stay non-allocatable (s2_allocatableSlots requires usefulCnt.isSaturateNegative, Ittage.scala:296).
required_result: After the second resetUsefulCnt pulse, every set of every bank receives a useful:=0 write before needReset clears (i.e. the second request restarts or re-queues a full sweep: sets 0..k-1 must be written again after the pulse).
observe: Waveform: io.update.resetUsefulCnt (IttageTable.scala:185) rising while needReset (IttageTable.scala:181) is already 1 and resetSet (IttageTable.scala:184) =/= 0; then count usefulCanReset (IttageTable.scala:182) cycles until resetFinish (IttageTable.scala:184): it is setsPerBank - k, not setsPerBank. Counters: ittage_us_tick_reset (IttageTable.scala:264) / ittage_reset_u (Ittage.scala:417) advance by more than the number of resetFinish events (no counter for resetFinish exists; add one or count falling edges of needReset); ittage_allocate (Ittage.scala:420) stays flat through the absorbed pulse.
notes: Sub-case 'pulse in the same cycle as resetFinish' HOLDS: when(resetUsefulCnt) has priority over .elsewhen(resetFinish) (IttageTable.scala:185-189), so needReset stays 1; the chisel3.util.Counter value wraps to 0 in the resetFinish cycle (setsPerBank is 128/256, power of two; library semantics, not in-tree), so the next cycle starts a full sweep at set 0. That timing is reachable: the tick-saturating update at cycle C makes tickCnt=255 at C+1, updateResetUsefulCnt=1 at C+1, table pulse at C+2 where update.valid=RegNext(updateMask at C+1) and req.fire may both be 0 while resetSet===setsPerBank-1. The pulse itself cannot be dropped: it sets needReset unconditionally and is one cycle wide (tickCnt.resetZero at Ittage.scala:397 overrides selfUpdate at :379 by last-connect, so 0->255 needs >=255 further increments). The only failing state class is 'pulse while needReset=1 and resetSet=k>0': the request is coalesced into the in-flight sweep and the portion 0..k-1 is silently dropped. Sweep stall under load is the enabler (usefulCanReset needs both no read and no update in the same cycle, IttageTable.scala:182), and the same load (dense mispredicted indirects without allocatable slots) is what drives tickCnt to 255 again. Whether this counts as a violation depends on R-ITTAGE-5 demanding a full sweep per saturation; the coalescing idiom is likely intentional, but the claim text ('the request is not forgotten') is false for the 0..k-1 portion.
